candidates.entry: long GLD when 12-month (252d) return > 0 AND 1-month (21d) return > 0; short GLD when 12-month return < 0 AND 1-month return < 0
candidates.exit: exit on 12-month momentum sign flip or 60 trading day hold (whichever first)
candidates.sizing: fixed 100% of capital per signal (long or short), no leverage
candidates.regime_filter: skip when GLD 90-day realized volatility > 25% annualized (avoid extreme vol regimes)
candidates.rationale: Time-series momentum on gold (GLD) should replicate the robust trend-following edge documented by Miffre & Rallis (2007), with gold's lower volatility and persistent trends likely yielding favorable risk-adjusted returns over 2020-2025.

candidates.entry: long GLD when 3-month futures curve slope (proxied by GLD price vs 3-month forward price from ETF structure) is backwardated (slope > 0); short when contango (slope < 0)
candidates.exit: exit on carry sign flip or 30 trading day hold
candidates.regime_filter: skip when GLD 60-day average daily volume < 5 million shares (low liquidity regime)
candidates.rationale: Carry strategy on gold using ETF structure as proxy for futures curve slope should capture the 0.8% monthly carry premium documented by Boons & Prado (2019), with gold's persistent backwardation periods providing positive roll yield.

candidates.entry: long DBA when 5-year price relative to 200-day moving average < 0.8 (cheap); short DBA when 5-year price relative to 200-day moving average > 1.2 (expensive)
candidates.exit: exit when price reverts to 0.95-1.05 of 200-day MA or 90 trading day hold
candidates.regime_filter: skip when DBA 200-day volatility > 30% annualized (avoid extreme agricultural shocks)
candidates.rationale: Value strategy on DBA (agricultural commodity ETF) using 5-year price relative to moving average should replicate Bianchi et al. (2018) 0.6% monthly alpha, with agricultural commodities exhibiting mean-reversion tendencies.

candidates.entry: long top 2 commodities by 12-month momentum (GLD, SLV, PPLT, PALL, CPER, DBA); short bottom 2 by 12-month momentum; equal-weight long/short
candidates.exit: rebalance monthly; exit all positions on rebalance day
candidates.sizing: equal-weight long/short, each leg 50% of capital (net zero beta)
candidates.regime_filter: skip when average cross-sectional dispersion of 12-month returns across universe < 5% (low momentum dispersion regime)
candidates.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum across commodity ETFs should capture the 0.8% monthly return documented by Asness et al. (2013), with diversification across 6 symbols reducing idiosyncratic risk and improving Sharpe ratio.

candidates.entry: long GLD when both 12-month momentum > 0 AND carry (proxied by 3-month forward curve slope) > 0; short when both < 0; else flat
candidates.exit: exit on either momentum or carry sign flip, or 45 trading day hold
candidates.regime_filter: skip when GLD 30-day correlation to SPY > 0.7 (high equity beta regime reduces commodity-specific edge)
candidates.rationale: Combined carry+momentum on gold should improve Sharpe ratio by 40% as per Boons & Prado (2019), with orthogonal signals reducing false positives and enhancing risk-adjusted returns.

notes_to_p3: Focus backtesting on GLD as primary symbol due to liquidity and clean ETF structure. For cross-sectional strategy, ensure rebalancing accounts for ETF trading costs (0.1-0.3% spread). The carry proxy using ETF structure may need calibration-use GLD's net asset value vs. spot gold as alternative. Monitor 2020 COVID vol spike and 2022 rate hike regimes as stress tests. If all strategies fail Tier-2 floors, consider NO_EDGE verdict for commodity ETFs due to structural decay of futures-based premia in ETF wrappers.
